Itinerary
a family trip to
中国
China, autumn 2027

Thirteen days together. Ten full days exploring Beijing, Zhangjiajie and Shanghai, plus travel days either side.

hosted by José Pina, the GOAT

Twelve of usfour cities, three stops,one big adventure

Beijing’s palaces and the Great Wall, the misty stone towers of Zhangjiajie, and the lights of Shanghai. Here’s everything you need to know.

Option 1: late September
Fri 17 to Wed 29 September 2027
Option 2: after Golden Week
Fri 8 to Wed 20 October 2027

still finalising which week, depending on a few people’s availability!

Hi everyone!

I’m so excited we’re doing this. I planned a trip to China in May 2026, so I’ve got some experience and lots of tips to share.

Most of all, I want this trip to be enjoyable for everyone. We’ll have plenty of free time to rest, explore or just do what we need. The itinerary here is a structure, not a strict schedule. Closer to the dates I’ll share a proper version with hotels, times and all the details.

I’m arranging transfers from the airports to the hotels too, so that part is sorted. My goal is to make this as easy and stress-free as possible.

That said, China is a very different country, and we need to be ready for lots of walking, some hiking and being exhausted at times! So I’m making goodie bags to keep us all feeling healthy. They’ll be waiting at our first hotel.

We have a full year of planning ahead, so please send me any suggestions, thoughts or wishes. I really want everyone to feel heard.

Margarida

How itall works

Who pays for what

José is being incredibly generous and is covering everyone’s flights, hotels, transfers and tours.

Anything extra is on you, so it’s worth saving up a little: your visa if you need one, travel insurance, your eSIM, snacks, drinks, shopping and anything outside the itinerary.

typical prices at the bottom of the page

Meals and family dinners

José is covering the meals we have together. Snacks, coffees and food outside the itinerary are each person’s own.

To say thank you, I thought it would be lovely for each couple or family group to take a turn paying for one family dinner. Don’t worry, meals in China are very affordable, around 10 to 15 euros per person.

Rooms

We’ll try our best to have two people per room. Depending on availability, some rooms may have two separate beds instead of one double.

Flights

  • Once everything is planned, I’ll send suggested flights so we all land at similar times
  • I’ll look for easy flights with relaxed layovers
  • If your layover is inside China, I’ll try to get each couple or group lounge access
  • Everyone flying from the same city travels together
  • I’ll send a few options and confirm with everyone before anything is bought

The itinerarya structure, not a schedule

The order of cities is set, the days are ideas, and there’s free time built in. Pick a date option, then tap any day for more.

day 1

Fly out

Flights from Lisbon, London, San Francisco and Boston, mostly overnight.

北京

Beijingpalaces, hutongs and the Great Wall

Days 2 to 5 · 4 nights

The capital. Imperial palaces, old hutong lanes, parks full of locals dancing and playing cards, and the Great Wall within driving distance. Four nights gives us three full days after we land.

day 2Land in Beijing and settle in
  • Transfer from the airport to the hotel (arranged)
  • Pick up your goodie bag at the hotel
  • Rest, then an easy dinner nearby
  • If you have energy, a short stroll through a hutong
day 3Forbidden City and Jingshan Park
  • Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City (bring your passport, tickets are in your name)
  • Jingshan Park for the view over the golden palace roofs
  • Welcome dinner: Peking duck
day 4The Great Wall
  • Mutianyu section: restored, less crowded and beautiful
  • Cable car up, so there’s no need for a long climb
  • For the brave: a toboggan ride back down
  • Free evening
day 5Temple of Heaven and a free afternoon
  • Temple of Heaven in the morning, when the park is full of locals doing tai chi and dancing
  • Afternoon free: the Summer Palace, the Lama Temple, shopping, or a nap
张家界

Zhangjiajiethe real Avatar mountains

Days 6 to 8 · 3 nights in Wulingyuan

Picture thousands of stone towers, some taller than skyscrapers, rising straight out of a misty forest. This is the place that inspired the floating mountains in Avatar, and it’s even more unreal in person.

We’ll ride a glass elevator straight up a cliff face, float over the peaks in cable cars, and walk a see-through glass path hanging off the side of a mountain. Clouds drift between the pillars, so the view changes every few minutes. We stay in one hotel in Wulingyuan, right by the park, for all three nights.

day 6Fly to Zhangjiajie
  • Morning flight from Beijing, about two and a half hours
  • Transfer to our hotel in Wulingyuan
  • Relaxed evening and an early night, the next two days are big ones
day 7Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
  • The Bailong Elevator: the world’s tallest outdoor lift, up a 326 metre cliff in under two minutes
  • Yuanjiajie and the Avatar Hallelujah Mountain viewpoints
  • Tianzi Mountain cable car over the peaks
  • Park buses link everything, so walking can be kept light if needed
day 8Tianmen Mountain
  • About an hour’s drive from Wulingyuan
  • One of the world’s longest cable car rides, up and over the mountains
  • The cliffside glass skywalk (if you dare to look down)
  • Heaven’s Gate, a giant natural arch through the mountain
  • Optional extra for thrill-seekers: the Grand Canyon glass bridge
上海

Shanghaiskylines, gardens and soup dumplings

Days 9 to 12 · 4 nights

A big, glamorous city to finish. The riverside skyline lit up at night, leafy old streets, amazing food, and easy day trips to gardens and canal towns.

day 9Fly to Shanghai
  • Flight from Zhangjiajie, about two hours
  • Evening walk along the Bund to see the skyline light up
day 10Old Shanghai
  • Yu Garden and the old town, with soup dumplings for lunch
  • Afternoon wandering the tree-lined streets of the former French Concession
  • Free evening
day 11Day trip
  • Suzhou’s classical gardens, about 30 minutes away by bullet train
  • Or the canal town of Zhujiajiao, with stone bridges and little boats
day 12Free day and farewell dinner
  • Free time: shopping, a massage, rest, or the view from the top of the Shanghai Tower
  • Farewell dinner all together
day 13

Fly home

Transfers to the airport and flights back to Lisbon, London, San Francisco and Boston.

Appsthe most important bit

read this!!

Google and our Western social media don’t work in China.

That means Google, Gmail, Google Maps, WhatsApp, Instagram and more are blocked. Don’t panic: I’ll give everyone a VPN to download before the trip so we can access everything, plus a proper guide on installing and using all of these apps. No need to do anything yet.

Alipay

pay for everything

Link your normal bank card and pay by scanning QR codes. Inside Alipay you can also open other apps to order food, call a taxi, buy transport tickets and more.

WeChat

messages and a wallet

China’s WhatsApp, and also a way to pay. Like Alipay, it has lots of mini apps inside for food, tickets and transport.

Paying with QR codes

so easy

Everything is payable with QR codes, from restaurants to street stalls: just scan and pay. If you’d like some cash just in case, that’s fine too.

DiDi

taxis, like Uber

Really cheap: around 2 euros for a 15 minute ride. You can also use it from inside Alipay.

eSIM

data on your phone

A digital SIM for internet while we’re there. I’ll help everyone get one, so no need to worry about it now.

Maps and translation

getting around

Apple Maps or Amap work well in China. A translation app with Chinese downloaded offline helps with menus and taxi drivers.

Good to knowthe things nobody tells you

Pack extra deodorant

It’s really hard to find in China. Bring enough for the whole trip.

For the ladies

Tampons are very hard to find, so bring your own just in case. Pads are easy to get.

Always carry tissues

Most public toilets don’t have toilet paper, and many are squat toilets, so get those legs ready! Hand sanitiser and wet wipes are your friends.

Power banks

You can rent power banks almost everywhere in the cities by scanning a QR code. Still, always carry your own just in case.

Chinese domestic flights are strict: power banks need a clear CCC (3C) safety mark and can’t be used during the flight. Check yours before we go.

Your passport is your ticket

Keep the real passport on you, not a photo. You’ll need it for hotels, trains, flights and most big sights.

A few more surprises

  • Drinks often come warm. Ask for ice if you want it
  • Don’t drink tap water. Bottled water is everywhere and cheap
  • People may ask for a photo with you. You’re basically famous
  • Electric scooters are silent, look both ways twice
  • Metro stations have bag scanners, like at airports
  • There’s no tipping
  • Crowds and queues can be intense, patience is key

What to pack

  • Really comfortable walking shoes, with lots of steps ahead
  • Light layers and a rain jacket, Zhangjiajie can be misty
  • Something warmer for the mountains and evenings
  • Plug adapter (China mostly uses Type A and Type I)
  • Any regular medication, in its original packaging
  • A small backpack for day trips

Visas and insurance

Each person sorts their own. What you need depends on your passport and the rules change often, so check the Chinese embassy or consulate website for your country. Your passport should be valid for six months after the trip. Get travel insurance that covers medical care abroad and cancellations.

Useful phrases

  • Hello: nǐ hǎo
  • Thank you: xiè xie
  • How much?: duō shǎo qián?
  • No spice please: bú yào là
  • Cheers: gān bēi
